fig1_hard_sphere_factor4.svg: Hard-sphere total cross-section (in units of the geometric disc $\pi a^2$) vs $ka$, from total_cross_section of phase_shifts_hard_sphere. As $ka\to0$ it tends to $4\pi a^2$ — FOUR times the classical shadow $\pi a^2$: a long-wavelength wave diffracts off the whole surface, and the $s$-wave ($\ell=0$, dashed) carries all of it. At high energy ever more partial waves switch on and $\sigma$ settles toward $2\pi a^2$.
fig2_born_yukawa_rutherford.svg: First-Born differential cross-section $|f(\theta)|^2$ for the Yukawa potential $V=\beta e^{-\mu r}/r$ at $k=2$, from born_amplitude_yukawa, as the screening $\mu$ shrinks. Each curve is strongly forward-peaked; the finite screening length $1/\mu$ keeps the forward ($\theta\to0$) value finite. As $\mu\to0$ the curves climb toward the bare-Coulomb rutherford_cross_section $\propto\sin^{-4}(\theta/2)$ (dashed), which diverges forward — the same $d\sigma/d\Omega$ classical mechanics gives.
